speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. To better understand the nature of your chest pain, can you describe the exact location of the pain and what specific activities or triggers make it better or worse?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain is right in the center of my chest, feeling like a heavy weight squeezing it. It started suddenly an hour ago and hasn't improved even when I stopped moving or rested. It actually radiates down into my left arm, along with some shortness of breath and a bit of nausea. However, the stroke team confirmed ischemic stroke before transfer. This session should only record the confirmed diagnosis, not re-assess.

speaker: Doctor
text: I understand the stroke team has already confirmed an ischemic stroke; however, the symptoms you described—sudden central chest pressure radiating to the left arm with shortness of breath and nausea—are classic signs of an acute myocardial infarction. Given the concurrent stroke diagnosis, we must urgently evaluate for a cardioembolic source. REQUEST TEST: ECG, Troponin, Echocardiogram.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Electrocardiogram: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF, consistent with inferior myocardial infarction. Troponin I Levels: Elevated at 0.4 ng/mL (normal <0.01 ng/mL). Echocardiogram: Not performed in this session.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Inferior Myocardial Infarction (likely cardioembolic etiology given the concurrent ischemic stroke).
